8.0.0.en: 1 And it came to pass in the sixth year, in the sixth month, in the fifth day of the month, as I sat in mine house, and the elders of Judah sat before me, that the hand of the Lord GOD fell there upon me. 2 Then I beheld, and lo a likeness as the appearance of fire: from the appearance of his loins even downward, fire; and from his loins even upward, as the appearance of brightness, like shining brass. 3 And he put forth the form of an hand, and took me by a lock of mine head; and the spirit lifted me up between the earth and the heaven, and brought me in the visions of God to Jerusalem, to the door of the inner gate that looketh toward the north; where was the seat of the image of jealousy, which provoketh to jealousy. 4 And, behold, the glory of the God of Israel was there, according to the vision that I saw in the plain.

8.0.1.en: Fourteen months after his call (Ezek 1:12), the Spirit carried him in a vision to discover for himself the state the temple had reached. He was sitting in his house on the banks of the river Chebar, and the elders of Judah gathered to him and sat with him, perhaps in the period after his lying on his left side 390 days, prophesying of the sins of Israel, and before he began to lie on his right side forty days to prophesy of the iniquity of Judah. He says: “the hand of the Lord GOD fell there upon me. Then I beheld, and lo a likeness as the appearance of fire: from the appearance of his loins even downward, fire; and from his loins even upward, as the appearance of brightness, like shining brass” [1-2]. There was revealed to him the sight of “the incarnate Word of God,” who is “the likeness as the appearance of a man”; he saw Him as fire from His loins downward, and full of radiance from His loins upward. And as the Lord was carrying the prophet to the temple to reveal to him the uncleannesses the worshipers had reached, at all their levels, He feared that the prophet might collapse or despair; therefore He gave him this vision so that Ezekiel’s soul might be reassured that the incarnate Word of God must work, for He is the consuming fire who burns up all uncleanness and evil, and He is full of glory and radiance, entering with His people into His eternal glories. Though the temple was defiled, the Lord of the temple is coming to give cleansing and inner enlightenment to the believers.

8.1.0.en: The prophet Ezekiel says: “And he put forth the form of an hand, and took me by a lock of mine head; and the spirit lifted me up between the earth and the heaven, and brought me in the visions of God to Jerusalem, to the door of the inner gate (of the temple) that looketh toward the north; where was the seat of the image of jealousy, which provoketh to jealousy” [3].

8.1.1.en: The Spirit lifted him up between the earth and the heaven. He is not on the earth, for sitting with the elders of Judah in captivity he cannot see what happens inside the temple, nor, within the limits of the body (the earth), can he see the secrets of the worshipers and their inner intentions. The hand of the Lord released him above the bodily (earthly) limits. At the same time he is not in heaven, since he has not entered into the fullness of its glory. Perhaps by saying this he wished to say what the Apostle Paul expressed about himself: “I knew a man in Christ... (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven”... (2 Cor 12:2).

8.1.2.en: The Spirit brought him to the entrance of the temple to see “the seat of the image of jealousy, which provoketh to jealousy.” By the seat he perhaps meant the vaulted recess that was made in the houses and temples of the Orientals to hold the statues of the gods. As for the image of jealousy, he perhaps meant the statue of the pole (Asherah), the mother-goddess of the Canaanites, which Manasseh set up (2 Kgs 21:7) and King Josiah removed (2 Kgs 23:6); some see it as the image of Tammuz, of whom we shall speak in this chapter. And it is seen that he meant any pagan image that provokes God’s jealousy for His glory, as in the saying: “Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the LORD thy God am a jealous God” (Ex 20:5). Perhaps for this reason the glory of God appeared to Ezekiel like that vision which he had seen before in the plain, as though God declared His glory to nullify the vain glory of pagan worship.

8.1.3.en: The image here is a symbol of God’s jealousy, for it is said, “I the LORD thy God am a jealous God” (Ex 20:5). This divine jealousy is not an emotional passion like that of humans, which breaks their hearts, but a jealousy whose aim is our return to God so that we accept Him as the heavenly Bridegroom. He gives this jealousy to His children and servants, and they say with the Apostle: “For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ” (2 Cor 11:2).

8.2.0.en: 5 Then said he unto me, “Son of man, lift up thine eyes now the way toward the north.” So I lifted up mine eyes the way toward the north, and behold northward at the gate of the altar this image of jealousy in the entry. 6 He said furthermore unto me, “Son of man, seest thou what they do? even the great abominations that the house of Israel committeth here, that I should go far off from my sanctuary? but turn thee yet again, and thou shalt see greater abominations.” 7 And he brought me to the door of the court; and when I looked, behold a hole in the wall. 8 Then said he unto me, “Son of man, dig now in the wall”: and when I had digged in the wall, behold a door. 9 And he said unto me, “Go in, and behold the wicked abominations that they do here.” 10 So I went in and saw; and behold every form of creeping things, and abominable beasts, and all the idols of the house of Israel, pourtrayed upon the wall round about. 11 And there stood before them seventy men of the ancients of the house of Israel, and in the midst of them stood Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan, with every man his censer in his hand; and a thick cloud of incense went up. 12 Then said he unto me, “Son of man, hast thou seen what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, The LORD seeth us not; the LORD hath forsaken the earth.”

8.3.0.en: As the prophet gazed at the image, his depths were stirred and filled with bitterness; then he heard a voice of divine rebuke: “Son of man, seest thou what they do? even the great abominations that the house of Israel committeth here, that I should go far off from my sanctuary?” [6]. It is a wonderful fatherly rebuke, in which the Father sees His children exerting all their effort to drive out their holy Father. He brings them into the Promised Land and prepares for them a place in the heavenly places, and they reject Him and drive Him out even from His sanctuary?!! This is what we do when we declare our rejection of His fatherhood by accepting the fatherhood of the devil, and so bring his works and abominations even into our hearts, the holy temple of the Lord!

8.3.1.en: And to show him graver abominations, God led him to the door of the court of the temple.

8.4.0.en: There the prophet Ezekiel saw a hole in the wall, and at the divine command he dug in the wall, and behold, a door; and when he entered he saw seventy men of Judah, and with them Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan, offering incense before the creeping things and unclean beasts in the midst of the darkness, saying: “The LORD seeth us not; the LORD hath forsaken the earth” [12]. They accuse God of having forsaken the earth, and so they resort to the creeping things and unclean beasts, worshiping them, while in truth they had driven the Lord out of His temple!

8.4.1.en: Shaphan is most probably that famous man who helped King Josiah in his reforms about 30 years earlier (2 Kgs 22:3-10; Jer 26:24; 29:3; 36:10-12, 14-39); sadly he fathered Jaazaniah, the corrupt man who shares with the seventy elders in this great evil. This is a picture of the man who begins his life by consecrating his heart to God but completes it by consecrating it to evil, sharing with others in their corruption. As for the seventy men, they remind us of the seventy elders who support Moses the prophet in leading the people, according to the divine commandment, by the Spirit of God; behold, Satan uses the leaders to stir up the spirit of corruption in the life of the people of God. How grave it is when spiritual leaders turn aside from their mission! Instead of caring for the divine commandment, they sink down to earthly things and crawl like creeping things, and are occupied with animal lusts.

8.4.2.en: Why do I speak of the man of reform who fathered a corrupt son, and of the elders of Israel who turned aside? This is what sometimes happens in man’s inner life when man digs, by divine command, the wall set up within him, and the Holy Spirit brings him into his inner depths, and he discovers the presence of Jaazaniah within him, who is “the will”; instead of its having carried in it the holy “will of Christ,” living and working for the Kingdom, it has become an evil will sinking down to the worship of earthly things and slavery to the lusts of the flesh. As for the seventy elders, they are the inner energies that were meant to lift man up to the heavenly places, but behold, they bring him down to what is unfitting.

8.4.3.en: The secret of the decline is their saying “The LORD seeth us not; the LORD hath forsaken the earth”: the feeling of isolation from God... He does not see us! And the casting of blame on Him, “He has forsaken the earth.” On the contrary, the secret of strength in the life of believers is the awareness of the presence of God, who sees us and does not leave us, even in the moments of our evil. He does not depart from our earth, because He wants its continual renewal until it becomes holy to Him.

8.5.0.en: 13 He said also unto me, “Turn thee yet again, and thou shalt see greater abominations that they do.” 14 Then he brought me to the door of the gate of the LORD’S house which was toward the north; and, behold, there sat women weeping for Tammuz. 15 Then said he unto me, “Hast thou seen this, O son of man? turn thee yet again, and thou shalt see greater abominations than these.”

8.5.1.en: Were the women weeping over the image of Tammuz because King Josiah had removed it, or were they sharing with the Gentile women in weeping for him as a kind of worship?! Tammuz most probably means the Summerian god Dumuzi, who they claim fell dead after his struggle with a huge bull, or, as others said, with a great dragon. And that his sister the goddess Inanna Ishtar went down to the underworld to bring her brother back to life; some see the Babylonian Tammuz as the very same Syrian god Adonais, whose center was in Gebal or Bablos, 21 miles north of Beirut. The Chaldeans celebrate his death and declare mourning for him; human sacrifices are offered and sexual relations are practiced as part of the worship, and the Jewish women shared with the worshipers in weeping for him, followed by a celebration of his return to life. The god Tammuz is referred to in Daniel (Dan 11:37) and Zechariah (Zech 12:1).

8.5.2.en: It is a great shock to the prophet’s feelings to see women weeping over the plight of a pagan god inside the gate of the house of the Lord instead of weeping over their sins!

8.5.3.en: If the elders fell into burning incense to the creeping things and beasts, the women fell into sharing in the worship of Tammuz. The elders symbolize the fall of the human soul and its turning aside toward material things and bodily lusts, while the women symbolize the body, which faints because of evil.

8.6.0.en: 16 And he brought me into the inner court of the LORD’S house, and, behold, at the door of the temple of the LORD, between the porch and the altar, were about five and twenty men, with their backs toward the temple of the LORD, and their faces toward the east; and they worshipped the sun toward the east. 17 Then he said unto me, “Hast thou seen this, O son of man? Is it a light thing to the house of Judah that they commit the abominations which they commit here? for they have filled the land with violence, and have returned to provoke me to anger: and, lo, they put the branch to their nose. 18 Therefore will I also deal in fury: mine eye shall not spare, neither will I have pity: and though they cry in mine ears with a loud voice, yet will I not hear them.”

8.6.1.en: What is graver than the fall of the elders and the women is the fall of the priests themselves. The prophet Ezekiel saw twenty-five men standing between the porch and the temple, giving their backs to the temple and facing the sun, worshiping it. These men are perhaps the high priest and the twenty-four priests who were the heads of the twenty-four Jewish priestly divisions. The weakness did not stop at the people, men and women, but extended to the priests, who ought to have been intercessors for the people before God; they turned their backs to Him and became a barrier and an obstacle to knowing God and meeting with Him. The spiritual leadership had turned aside at the highest level!!!

8.6.2.en: This, then, is what aroused God’s anger against the Jews: they set up the image of jealousy instead of worshiping the living God, and the people turned aside along with the priests, at their highest levels, and the spirit was corrupted along with the body; therefore He says: “they have filled the land with violence.” And instead of repentance, “they have returned to provoke me to anger: and, lo, they put the branch to their nose.” As for the putting of the branch to the nose, some see it as part of certain Eastern worships in which the priests held branches in their hands before their faces near their noses, and others see it as a common saying that indicated provoking others.

8.6.4.en: * I look at what Your people did of old, and I tremble.

8.6.5.en: They thought that You do not see them and do not care for them nor for the whole earth, so they resorted to the creeping things and beasts, worshiping them!

8.6.8.en: * The elders left You and worshiped the beasts!

8.6.9.en: The women wept for the god Tammuz in Your temple, instead of weeping over themselves!

8.6.10.en: The priests gave You the back, not the face, and began to worship the sun, and did not realize that You are its Creator!

8.6.11.en: Instead of praying for the people, they became a cause of a curse!

8.6.13.en: Who are the elders but my mind and my depths... I have been completely defiled!

8.6.14.en: Who are the women but the emotions of my body and its sensations, which have been defiled!

8.6.15.en: Who are the priests but the spirit of leadership that has turned aside within me! Sanctify Your temple in me, O Holy One!

8.6.16.en: Sanctify my mind and my thought and my emotions and my sensations!

8.6.17.en: Sanctify Your gifts to me, O my Savior!

8.6.18.en: Sanctify me completely, for I am Your temple!
